walkthrough:
**Why three digits**

The members are numbered 1 to 654. The biggest number, 654, has **3 digits**, so we read the random digits in **groups of 3**. Each group is a possible member number.

Because the secretary is choosing a sample without choosing anyone twice, we will skip a group if it is too big (more than 654) or if it repeats a member already chosen.

**Write the digits as one long line**

Remove the gaps in the first line of the table so the digits run on:

$$1096\ 4357\ 3765\ 0431\ 0928\ 9264 \;\longrightarrow\; 109643573765043109289264$$

Now cut this into groups of three, starting at the left:

$$109 \mid 643 \mid 573 \mid 765 \mid 043 \mid 109 \mid 289 \mid 264$$

Quick check: the first two groups are 109 and 643, exactly the first two members in the question. So we have started in the right place.

**Work through the next groups one at a time**

Continue from the third group, asking two questions each time: "is it 654 or smaller?" and "is it new?"

- $573$: this is below 654 and not used yet, so **member 573 is chosen**. (This earns the first B1.)

- $765$: this is bigger than 654, so there is no such member. **Reject it.**

- $043$: below 654 and new. It is member number 43 (we drop the leading zero), so **member 43 is chosen**. (Second B1.)

- $109$: this is below 654, but it is the first member we already chose. **Reject the repeat.**

- $289$: below 654 and new, so **member 289 is chosen**. (Third B1.)

We now have the three members we need, so we stop.

**Final answer**

The next three members in the sample are:

$$573,\quad 43,\quad 289$$

(The mark scheme also accepts 043 for the second one, and it allows a different correct use of the table such as 573, 650, 431.)
